extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a publicly available benchmark dataset for Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). The dataset contains 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class.
extraction.creator: Northwestern Polytechnical University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth, which maps the Earth via superimposition of images from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and GIS onto a 3D globe. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions worldwide under various weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted and formatted with a fixed size of 256×256 pixels in the RGB color space, with spatial resolutions varying from approximately 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene classes were selected by compiling 30 widely-used categories from existing datasets and 15 classes from literature searches on Web of Science and Google Scholar, totaling 45 classes (covering land use/land cover, man-made objects, and landscape nature objects). Annotation and selection of 700 images per class was carried out by experts in remote sensing image interpretation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The classes of island, lake, mountain, and snowberg have lower spatial resolutions compared to the other scene classes which range from 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and benchmarking algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification, including handcrafted feature-based methods, unsupervised feature learning, and deep learning models.
